boundary_rationale: This unit opens the whole triple acrostic at its own tier-1 threshold: the geber's first-person onset is spliced at byte tier as אֲנִ֤י הַגֶּ֨בֶר֙ (oshb:Lam.3.1, byte tier), matched by the WEB witness “I am the man” (web:Lam.3.1). The span covers three consecutive triplets of the ch-3 triple acrostic in the witness's own letter order: alef א (3:1-3), bet ב (3:4-6) and gimel ג (3:7-9). This span's own close sits on the gimel triplet's own letter boundary at Lam.3.9. Across the nine verses the geber narrates the same first-person register of divine-agency affliction imagery, darkness, a hand turned against him, broken bones, a wall and a chain, a shut prayer, and crooked paths, naming no addressee across the span. Whether this first-person speaker is an individual or a collective persona is held here as a disputed literary question that this span does not decide.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the alef and bet triplets (Lam.3.1-Lam.3.6) off as a shorter opening unit was considered because their own affliction imagery (darkness, a hand turned against him, broken bones) forms a self-contained six-verse catalogue distinct from the imprisonment imagery (a wall, a chain, a shut prayer) that opens with the gimel triplet at Lam.3.7; it was rejected because the same first-person register continues from the bet triplet into the gimel triplet, addressed to nobody in particular, just as it does within the earlier triplets themselves.
